evidence.title: Instagram
evidence.description: In many real estate projects, developers used to register each building under a separate RERA number, launching towers in phases over time. As a result, the possession timelines also varied across buildings. Technically, if a developer completes a particular tower as per the promised RERA timeline and obtains Occupancy Certificate (OC) for that building, they are eligible to issue possession for that tower even if the rest of the project is still under construction. This is known as Part OC, and it cannot be rejected if the RERA commitments for that specific tower have been met. Buyers who accepted agreements under that particular RERA number are legally bound to take possession if the OC has been issued and the building is ready to occupy, provided there are no defects. [...] Watch our full discussion in Sawal Jawab Episode-192 on YouTube for more insights! #saudagharpune #pune #punevibes #punediaries #reelsitfeelsit #trendingvideo #viralvideo #viralshorts #reelsinstagram #foryou #PartOC #OCExplained #RERAIndia #RealEstateIndia #FlatPossession #Maharera #HomeBuyersGuide #PartOccupancyCertificate #RealEstateFacts #OCRules #HousingProjects #DeemedConveyance #OCClarification #PropertyLawIndia #RealEstateAwarenes [...] Part OC is common in large-scale projects that are built in phases. Developers often design the entire layout spanning 30 to 50 acres with dedicated segments for amenities, residential clusters, and open spaces, and then deliver towers in batches. Even in such cases, Part OC is issued based on individual land parcels or segments. Once a tower or a group of towers receives Part OC, a cooperative housing society can be formed. That society can eventually claim deemed conveyance and assert its legal rights over the land parcel, even if the overall project is incomplete. Therefore, buyers can take possession under Part OC, and later, through the society, pursue their rights and responsibilities as per law.
